items.readable_text:
Content:
Remember that when we multiply a decimal by a power of ten, we shift the decimal place to the right by the number of zeros in the power of ten.

Content:
When the power of ten is written in exponent form, the exponent tells us the number of places to shift the decimal point.

Content:
For instance, to find [MATH: 47 \times 10^{1}], we first rewrite [MATH: 10^1] as [MATH: 1] followed by a block of [MATH: 1] zero:
[MATH: 1]

Content:
Since we're multiplying by [MATH: 10] and [MATH: 10] has [MATH: \color{blue} 1] zero, we move the decimal point [MATH: \color{blue}1] place to the right.

Content:
[MATH: 47.0 \rightarrow 470]

Content:
Therefore,

Content:
[MATH: 47 \times 10^{1} = 470 \, .]
